misclassified_entities.reason: EVM contract caller is internal to EVM execution context. Any contract or EOA invoking a precompile via CALL opcode is part of normal EVM operation, not an external entity. The calldata and execution context are internal to transaction processing.
misclassified_entities.correct_modeling: The precompile input validation should model the calldata as data flowing through EVM execution rather than from an external entity. The true external boundary is at transaction submission.

trusted_external_entities.name: DApp (Batch Transaction Submitter)
trusted_external_entities.description: Decentralized application submitting batched calls via wallet RPC with flow control parameters
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: DApps are arbitrary web applications outside the wallet's control. They may attempt to submit malicious batches, exploit flow control parameters, or manipulate atomicity settings. No authentication or accountability mechanism exists.
data_provided: call sequence with data and value
attack_vectors: Submitting malicious call sequences that exploit state dependencies
Manipulating flow control to achieve partial execution for exploit
Requesting atomicity levels beyond actual requirements to cause failures

trusted_external_entities.name: JSON-RPC Client
trusted_external_entities.description: External application or user querying block information via JSON-RPC eth_getBlockByNumber
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: RPC clients are anonymous external entities. They can craft arbitrary queries and cannot be authenticated. The node must validate all request parameters and never trust client-provided data.
attack_vectors: Crafted requests attempting to cause resource exhaustion
Probing for chain state or fork information
Malformed parameters to trigger error conditions

trusted_external_entities.name: Web Application (Token Watch Requester)
trusted_external_entities.description: External website or decentralized application requesting wallet track a token via wallet_watchAsset
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: DApps can be malicious and attempt phishing attacks by requesting wallets track fake tokens with similar names/symbols to legitimate ones. Image URLs can be used for SSRF attacks. All provided data must be validated.
attack_vectors: Token impersonation/phishing (similar names to real tokens)
Scam token tracking to deceive users about holdings

trusted_external_entities.name: Contract Deployer
trusted_external_entities.description: EOA or contract initiating contract creation via transaction or CREATE/CREATE2 opcodes
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Contract deployers are arbitrary external parties. They control init code and deployment parameters but cannot be trusted to behave correctly. The collision detection must enforce security properties regardless of deployer intent.
attack_vectors: Attempting to deploy at known addresses to exploit expectations
CREATE2 salt manipulation to target specific addresses
Front-running deployments to occupy target addresses

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious Actor (Collision Attacker)
trusted_external_entities.description: Attacker attempting to replace existing contract code via address collision
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: This entity is explicitly modeled as an adversary. They actively attempt to violate the security property of code immutability. The collision detection mechanism is specifically designed to defeat this threat.
attack_vectors: Computing address collisions to overwrite legitimate contracts
Exploiting any gap between address computation and collision check
Leveraging CREATE2 determinism to pre-compute collision addresses

security_assumptions: Wallet validates all flow control parameters against its capabilities
Wallet enforces correct atomicity semantics for the requested level
DApp cannot observe wallet behavior before response (anti-fingerprinting)
Wallet correctly reports supported atomicity levels
Wallet rejects unsupported atomicity rather than downgrading silently
Atomicity guarantees are maintained even during chain reorgs (for strict mode)
Node validates block number format before processing
Fork status determination is accurate for baseFee inclusion
Response does not leak internal state beyond requested block data
Wallet validates address checksum format
Wallet returns immediately to prevent fingerprinting
User prompt is asynchronous and independent of RPC response
Wallet validates URI scheme against whitelist (https, ipfs, data)
Wallet blocks requests targeting localhost/internal services (SSRF prevention)
Wallet performs phishing detection against known token lists
Collision check occurs before any init code execution
Address computation is deterministic and verifiable
Both nonce and code checks must pass for deployment to proceed
Collision detection always runs before init code execution
Non-zero nonce OR non-zero code triggers collision failure
Attack is blocked regardless of computational resources used for collision

coverage_analysis.notes: EXT-EVM-CALLER from EIP-197 is internal to EVM and reclassified. All true external entities (dApps, RPC clients, deployers, attackers) have corresponding boundary edges. Multiple boundary edges exist for EXT-DAPP entities due to distinct security concerns per subgraph.
